subject: Fitting a Hierarchical Bayesian model with spatial component using R-INLA

messages.author: 14ee5df6121f437e
messages.subject: Fitting a Hierarchical Bayesian model with spatial component using R-INLA
parts:
Hello all, 

I have to fit couple of customized Bayesian Hierarchical Models. So I was wondering if there is any easy ways to do those in R-Inla? One of my model specification is stated below:

#################################################################################################################
Y_i ~ N(mu_i, sigma_i^2) # i=1, 2, ..., 517 areas
mui= X*beta+ psi_i +epsilon_i  # beta be the fixed covariate effect, psi_i is the spatial random effect and epsilon_i is non-spatial residual

#priors: 
epsilon_i ~(iid) N(0, 1/sigma_epsilon_i)
psi_i ~ MVN (nu, tau*Sigma) #tau>0 is the precision parameter that controls the overall variability of psi_i 
Sigma_ij=exp[-(vd_ij)^k] #  k (0<k<2, usually taken as k=2) provides the extent of spatial smoothing and d_ij denotes the distances between centroids of areas i and j

#Hyperpriors: the hyperpriors for 
sigma_i^2 ~ 2* S_i^2/Chisq(2) # Si^2 be the sample variances of Y_i
sigma_epsilon_i~ Gamma(0.5,0.0005)
tau ~ Ga,mma(0.001,0.001)
k~Unif(0.05,1.95)
v~Unif(0.05,20)
############################################################################################################################

Can anyone suggest me the formula or command I need to use for fitting this type of models in R-INLA? 

Thanks and regards,
Farzana.

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Fitting a Hierarchical Bayesian model with spatial component using R-INLA
parts:
People don't usually ask for models like this since the mean-model mu_i and the variance model sigma_i are too confounded to be identifiable.

If you have a massive amount of data (in the right sense, whatever that is in this case) you may try to ad-hoc estimate sigma_i, and then use INLA with those estimates as known fixed values.

Best,
Haakon
